newsitem.title: USA: FDIC sells 14 mln Washington Mutual shares.
newsitem.headline: FDIC sells 14 mln Washington Mutual shares.

text.p: Federal Deposit Insurance Corp said Thursday it had sold 14 million shares of Washington Mutual Inc stock for $47.50 a share, or $665 million.
The FDIC said in a statement it received the stock Dec 20 in exchange for warrants it held in N.A. Capital Holdings, parent of American Savings Bank F.A. of Irvine, California.
Seattle-based thrift holding company Washington Mutual acquired Keystone Holdings Inc, parent of N.A. Capital Holdings Inc, on the same date.
Proceeds from the underwriting will go to the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corp (FSLIC) Resolution Fund and will reduce the cost of one of the largest thrift failures on record, the FDIC said.

FSLIC received an interest in N.A. Capital Holdings following the failure of American Savings in December 1988. In May 1996, Keystone approached the FDIC to restructure its warrant agreement in N.A. Capital Holdings, it said.
